requiredDisclosures: Notice must state the specific reason for eviction
Notice must include the exact amount of rent owed (for pay-or-quit)
Notice must be served properly: personal delivery, substituted service, or posting and mailing
For properties built before 1978, lead paint disclosure required
Under AB 1482 (Tenant Protection Act), landlord must state just cause for eviction if property is covered
illegalReasons: Tenant complained to a government agency about habitability or building code violations
Tenant organized or participated in a tenant union
Discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, source of income, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, age, or ancestry
retaliationProtections: California Civil Code Section 1942.5 prohibits retaliatory evictions
If tenant complained about habitability within 180 days before notice, retaliation is presumed
Landlord must prove non-retaliatory motive if evicting within 180 days of tenant complaint
ab1482Coverage: Properties built after 2005 are exempt. Single-family homes and condos are exempt if owner provides written notice. Duplexes where owner occupies one unit are exempt.
notes: California's Tenant Protection Act (AB 1482) requires 'just cause' for eviction in covered properties
Relocation assistance of 1 month's rent required for no-fault evictions in covered properties
Self-help evictions (changing locks, removing belongings) are illegal — tenant can sue for actual damages + $100/day
Waiving tenant rights in a lease is void and unenforceable under California law
COVID-19 protections may still apply in some jurisdictions — check local ordinances
